transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. It's very nice to meet you, and thank you so much for fitting me in. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time with this. 

Well... I hope I'm explaining this right, but what made me come in is that my eating has gotten, well, all turned around lately. It's a little silly, really. Some days I just forget to eat lunch completely. And then... I'm a bit embarrassed to admit this part, because I know better, but other days I'll just stand right at the kitchen counter eating crackers and sweets. And the funny thing is, nothing even tastes right to me anyway. 

Is that... does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information to start with.
How often have you been experiencing these changes in your eating habits, and how long has this been going on?

Well, let's see... I hope I'm remembering this correctly for you. It's been, oh, about a year and five months now. I'm sorry it's taken me so long to come in about it, I just kept thinking it would sort itself out, you know? 

It started right around the time my sister's health took a very serious turn. I've been so worried about her, and I suppose I just let my own routines slip a little bit. It's nothing terribly drastic, just... you know, happening off and on since then. I hope that's the kind of timeline you were looking for? I want to make sure I'm giving you all the right details.

Can you describe what typically goes through your mind when you're standing at the counter eating crackers and sweets? Is it more out of stress, boredom, comfort, or something else that you can put into words?

Well, oh goodness, it's a little hard to put into words. I suppose... I suppose I wouldn't call it stress, exactly. I mean, everyone has stress, don't they? I don't want to make it sound like I can't handle things. 

It's just... well, maybe it's more of a comfort thing? Or just something to do with my hands when my mind is wandering. I just sort of find myself there, and it's easier than making a whole proper meal just for myself, especially when things don't taste quite right anyway. It's really just a silly little habit I've picked up, nothing to be too concerned about, I'm sure. 

Do you... do you think that's normal? Or is that the kind of thing that usually means someone is stressed? I just want to make sure I'm answering you properly.
Have you noticed that you don't enjoy things as much as you used to, or that you've lost interest in activities you once found pleasurable?

Oh... well, I suppose I have been a little less active lately. I hope that doesn't make me sound terribly lazy. I used to really, really look forward to my watercolor class, and the quilting circle, and my book club. I always had such a lovely time. 

But lately... well, it's a bit embarrassing to admit, but I'll get my things all ready, and then I often just leave my bag right there by the door. I just... I just can't seem to make myself care quite enough to actually go. 

It sounds awful when I say it out loud, doesn't it? Like I'm just being ungrateful for my hobbies. I just hope I'm giving you the right sort of answers. Do you think that's just a normal part of getting a bit older?
Have you been feeling down or sad most of the time, even when there's no clear reason for it?

Oh, dear... well, I really hate to sound like a complainer. I know I have so much to be thankful for, so I feel a bit guilty even admitting it to you. But... well, yes, I suppose I have been feeling a little down. 

It's mostly in the mornings. I'll wake up with this... this heavy, sort of low feeling. It almost feels like the color has just gone right out of the day before I even manage to get dressed. I try my best to shake it off, I really do, and I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself. 

Does... does that make sense? Or am I just making a fuss out of nothing? I hope I'm explaining it the right way for you, doctor.
Have you noticed that you feel tired or lacking in energy most days, even if you’ve had a good night’s sleep?

Oh, my energy... well, I wouldn't say I'm completely exhausted all the time. I certainly don't want to give you the impression that I'm just lying in bed all day long. I do try to keep up with things as best I can. 

I suppose... well, maybe I do feel a little more tired than I used to. But at my age, isn't that just to be expected? I mean, a 74-year-old woman isn't going to have the energy of a teenager, right? I just figure I need to pace myself a bit more. 

I don't think it's anything too unusual, really. Do you... do you find that most people my age mention feeling a little less energetic? I just want to make sure I'm not making a mountain out of a molehill here.
Have you found yourself feeling more guilty or critical of yourself lately, or like you’re not living up to your own expectations, even when there’s no clear reason for it?

Oh, goodness... well, I don't think I'm overly critical of myself. I mean, I certainly try to be a good person and do what's right. I hope I don't come across as someone who's constantly complaining about themselves. 

I suppose... well, sometimes I do feel bad about leaving my bags by the door and missing my classes, like I mentioned earlier. I feel a bit guilty that I'm letting my friends down, or that I'm wasting the day. But I think anyone would feel a little bad about that, don't you? 

I really try to focus on the positive and not be too hard on myself. I hope that's the right way to look at it. Does that sound like a normal amount of guilt to you, doctor? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the answers you need.
Have you noticed that you've been moving more slowly than usual, or on the contrary, that you can't sit still and feel restless or fidgety?

Oh, well... I really hate to keep blaming my age, and I certainly don't want you to picture me just shuffling around helplessly. I do try to keep active! But... well, I suppose my body does feel a little slowed down lately. 

It just seems like it takes me twice as long to do simple things now, like crossing the living room or... or even just buttoning my sweater in the morning. I try not to let it frustrate me too much. 

But then, on the other hand, sometimes I do the exact opposite. I'll catch myself just pacing around the house, walking back and forth with the same papers in my hand, feeling a bit restless. 

I know that probably sounds a bit silly, being slow one minute and pacing the next. Is that... is that the sort of thing you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of examples, doctor.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or weight over the past year or so?

Oh, well... I do try to keep up good habits, I really do. I hope I don't sound like I'm just completely neglecting myself. But... well, actually, my eating is sort of what made me finally come in to see someone. It's just gotten all... turned around lately. 

Some days, I'll just completely forget to have lunch. I just don't even think about it. And then other days... well, I feel a little embarrassed to admit this, but I'll catch myself just standing at the kitchen counter, eating crackers and sweets. And the funny thing is, nothing even really tastes right to me anymore. 

I know I shouldn't be snacking like that instead of having a proper meal, and I do try to do better. Do you... do you think that's the kind of thing you need for your notes, doctor? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you noticed any loss of appetite or any significant weight loss over the past year?

Oh, I... I think we might have just talked about this a little bit, didn't we? I hope I didn't confuse things by bringing it up too early. 

Like I was saying, my eating habits are really what made me decide I should probably come in and talk to someone. It's just all gotten a bit turned around. I certainly haven't stopped eating altogether—I do try to take care of myself! But yes, some days I'll just completely forget to have lunch. It just slips my mind entirely. 

And then... well, like I mentioned, other days I'll just stand at the counter having crackers and sweets, even though nothing really tastes right to me anymore. I haven't been keeping track of my weight on a scale, so I don't want to give you the wrong idea about losing a specific number of pounds. 

I hope it's okay that I'm sort of repeating myself. Did I answer that the right way for you, doctor? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful.
Have you had any thoughts about life not being worth living, or found yourself wishing you would just fall asleep and not wake up?

Oh, my... well, I certainly don't want you to think I'm... I'm not ungrateful for my life, I promise you that. I know I have a lot to be thankful for, and I would never, ever do anything to hurt myself. I don't have any sort of plan like that. 

But... well, since you're asking, and I do want to be completely honest with you... sometimes, when things just feel so heavy, I do have this thought. I catch myself thinking that... well, that if I just went to sleep and didn't wake up the next morning, it might actually be a bit of a relief. Not just for me, but... maybe for everyone else, too. So I wouldn't be such a bother.

I hope that doesn't sound too terrible to say out loud. I feel awful even admitting it. Is that... is that the kind of thing you need to know, doctor? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions properly without sounding too... too dramatic.
How many days out of the week would you say you feel that low, heavy feeling you mentioned in the morning—nearly every day, most days, or only occasionally?

Oh, goodness... well, I really do try to put on a brave face and just get on with things. I don't want to sound like a complainer, because I know everyone has their bad days. 

But... if I'm being completely honest with you... I'd have to say it's most mornings. It's just this... this heavy, low feeling right when I wake up. It almost feels like all the color has just gone right out of the day before I even have a chance to get dressed. 

I always try my very best to shake it off, though, I promise! I don't just sit around dwelling on it if I can help it. I hope I'm answering this the way you need me to, doctor. Is that helpful for your notes?
Have you found yourself feeling like you’re not worth much, or that you’re letting people down even when they haven’t said anything to make you feel that way?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean... I know I just said a moment ago that sometimes I worry about being a bother, but I certainly don't feel like I'm not worth anything. Oh, goodness, I hope it doesn't sound boastful to say, but I really do try my very best to be a good person and help out where I can. 

And I don't think I'm letting people down... at least, I certainly hope I'm not! I always try to be very careful about being reliable for my friends and family. I don't walk around feeling like a disappointment to them. I really do try to keep a good attitude about my own worth, even on the tough days. 

Is it okay that I don't have that particular feeling, doctor? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information and not messing up your evaluation.

Can you tell me a bit more about how you feel when you think about your watercolor class, quilting circle, and book club? Is it that you don’t feel like going because you don’t enjoy them as much anymore, or is it more about not having the energy or motivation to go?

Oh... well... it's a little embarrassing to admit, to be perfectly honest. I don't want you to think I'm just being lazy or antisocial, because I really do love the ladies in those groups. They're wonderful people. 

But lately... well, it's not exactly that I'm too tired, though I suppose I am a bit. It's more that... I just can't seem to muster up the same enthusiasm I used to have for them. I used to look forward to watercolor class and the quilting circle all week. And the book club! I used to read the books so carefully. 

But now... I don't know what's wrong with me. I'll get all my things ready, and I'll leave my bag right there by the front door, fully intending to go... and then the time comes, and I just... I look at the bag, and I just can't make myself care enough to walk out the door. It just doesn't bring me that same joy right now. 

I feel terrible about it, I really do. I hate missing out and I hope they don't think I'm ignoring them. Does that make sense, doctor? I hope I'm explaining the difference properly. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of what's happening.

Can you tell me how you feel when you look at your bag by the door for watercolor class, quilting circle, or book club? Has it become harder to feel excited or motivated about attending these activities at all?

Oh, dear, I know I just mentioned this, and I really hope I don't sound like a broken record... I don't want to waste your time repeating myself. 

But yes, it's... it's just as I was saying. I'll get everything together for the watercolor class or the book club, and I leave the bag right there by the door. I used to be so eager to go, I really did! But lately, when it's time to leave, I just look at the bag and... I just can't seem to find that spark of excitement anymore. I just can't make myself care enough to actually go out the door. 

I know it sounds awful, and I really do try to push myself, I promise. I don't want to be one of those people who just gives up on their hobbies. Is it normal to feel this way sometimes, doctor? I just hope I'm being helpful by explaining it again.
Would you say that you no longer enjoy your hobbies, like watercolor painting, quilting, or book club, as much as you used to, even when you do attend?

Oh, goodness... I know we keep coming back to this, and I hope I'm not frustrating you by not giving a simple yes or no. I really am trying to be as helpful as I can be. 

But... well, yes, I suppose that's the truth of it. Even when I do manage to go, it's just... it's not the same. I used to just love sitting with the ladies and chatting over our quilting, or discussing the books... but lately, it's like that joy is just missing. It's exactly why I end up leaving my bag by the door so often now. I just can't seem to make myself care enough to go, because I know I won't feel that same happiness when I get there. 

I feel so guilty admitting that out loud. It sounds so ungrateful, doesn't it? I really don't want you to think I'm a negative person, doctor. I've always tried to look on the bright side. Is it alright that I'm feeling this way? I hope I'm giving you the right answers.
Would you say that you no longer enjoy your hobbies, like watercolor painting, quilting, or book club, as much as you used to, even when you do attend?

Oh, dear... I'm so sorry, I think you might have just asked me that, didn't you? I hope my memory isn't frustrating you, I know you have so many patients to see and I don't want to take up too much of your time. 

But, um... yes, I suppose it's just like I was saying. It's embarrassing to admit, but I just don't have that same enthusiasm. I used to really look forward to watercolor class, the quilting circle, and my book club. I'd be so excited all week. But now... well, I often just leave my bag right by the front door. I look at it, and I just can't make myself care enough to actually go. 

I really hope that makes sense, doctor. I'm trying my best to explain it clearly for you. Am I doing okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to help me.
Would you say that your low mood in the mornings lasts throughout most of the day, nearly every day?

Oh, um... yes, I suppose that's right. I really hope I'm not sounding like a complainer, doctor. I know so many people have it worse, and I try to count my blessings, I really do. 

But... well, most mornings I wake up with this... this heavy, low feeling. It's almost like the color has just gone out of the day before I even get dressed. And... well, it does tend to stick around for most of the day, pretty much every day lately. I try to put on a brave face, of course, I don't want to bring anyone else down. Is it okay that I'm feeling that way? I hope I'm giving you the right information.
